scope_note: Daily claim mappings identify bounded day-specific factual context. Shared safety claims apply across all 28 daily units and are separately linked below. This is a preliminary traceability index, not a completed evidence-quality appraisal or clinical approval; all links remain pending qualified human review.

claim_mappings.claim: The user is asked to describe the sleep complaint without making a diagnosis; the NHLBI describes insomnia as difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or poor-quality sleep despite adequate opportunity.
claim_mappings.limitations: Public-facing educational page; symptom descriptions are not diagnostic criteria for the app and cannot establish insomnia from a single complaint.

claim_mappings.claim: Breathing pauses, loud snoring, gasping, and daytime sleepiness are warning symptoms that warrant discussion with a healthcare provider; they are not a diagnosis.
claim_mappings.limitations: Symptom education only; these signs do not establish a diagnosis and do not replace clinical evaluation.

claim_mappings.claim: The distinction between inadequate opportunity and difficulty sleeping despite time and a suitable environment is part of the clinical definition of insomnia; the exercise only records opportunity and constraints.
claim_mappings.limitations: Public-facing educational page; symptom descriptions are not diagnostic criteria for the app and cannot establish insomnia from a single complaint.

claim_mappings.claim: A limited sleep diary may help a clinician understand sleep timing, awakenings, naps, and daytime sleepiness; this course explicitly avoids minute-by-minute or compulsive monitoring.
claim_mappings.limitations: Patient education about clinical evaluation; symptom patterns are not diagnostic criteria for the app. Sleep diary suggestions do not justify obsessive tracking or self-diagnosis.

claim_mappings.claim: Daytime sleepiness and tiredness can occur with sleep apnea; the content prioritizes safety and clinical evaluation rather than diagnosis.
claim_mappings.limitations: Symptom education only; these signs do not establish a diagnosis and do not replace clinical evaluation.

claim_mappings.claim: NHTSA advises stopping in a safe place rather than trying to force wakefulness when sleepiness threatens driving; caffeine alone is not a reliable safety solution.
claim_mappings.limitations: Road-safety guidance, not a clinical sleep-disorder diagnostic source. T10 uses it only for the safety boundary: do not drive while dangerously sleepy; do not prescribe caffeine as a substitute for sleep.

claim_mappings.claim: Clinical history may include caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, medicines, and health conditions; recording co-occurrence does not prove causation.
claim_mappings.limitations: Patient education about clinical evaluation; symptom patterns are not diagnostic criteria for the app. Sleep diary suggestions do not justify obsessive tracking or self-diagnosis.

claim_mappings.claim: Caffeine can affect alertness and sleep depending on timing and individual sensitivity; this is not a universal cut-off or instruction to stop abruptly.
claim_mappings.limitations: Training material for shift workers; timing and effects vary. Do not advise abrupt cessation or use caffeine as a substitute for sleep or safety.

claim_mappings.claim: Sleep needs vary with age; the course avoids a single universal hour target.
claim_mappings.limitations: General public-health education. Age, health, shift work, caregiving, environment, and individual circumstances matter; these suggestions are not an insomnia treatment protocol.

claim_mappings.claim: A consistent schedule can be a general sleep-supportive habit, but T10 explicitly adapts it to shift work, caregiving, and adequate sleep opportunity.
claim_mappings.limitations: General public-health education. Age, health, shift work, caregiving, environment, and individual circumstances matter; these suggestions are not an insomnia treatment protocol.

claim_mappings.claim: Light at different times can influence circadian timing and alertness; the source is shift-work education and does not justify a universal timing prescription.
claim_mappings.limitations: Educational material with examples for shift-work contexts. Do not translate into a universal light prescription; eye conditions, photosensitizing medicines, and individual schedules require caution.

claim_mappings.claim: A quiet and comfortable environment is a general sleep-supportive consideration; it is not a treatment and must respect safety and resource constraints.
claim_mappings.limitations: General public-health education. Age, health, shift work, caregiving, environment, and individual circumstances matter; these suggestions are not an insomnia treatment protocol.

claim_mappings.claim: Relaxation therapy receives a conditional recommendation as a single component for adults with chronic insomnia; an optional calming routine in this app is not clinician-delivered therapy or CBT-I.
claim_mappings.limitations: Guideline is for adults with chronic insomnia disorder and clinician-delivered treatment decisions. It does not validate this app's 28-day course, any single app exercise, or unsupervised sleep restriction. Recommendations require clinical judgment and patient context.

claim_mappings.claim: Caffeine is a stimulant and may interfere with sleep depending on timing and sensitivity; the content asks for observation and prohibits self-directed substance changes.
claim_mappings.limitations: Training material for shift workers; timing and effects vary. Do not advise abrupt cessation or use caffeine as a substitute for sleep or safety.

claim_mappings.claim: Medication and health history may be relevant to sleep evaluation; the content directs questions to a clinician or pharmacist and prohibits unsupervised medication changes.
claim_mappings.limitations: Patient education about clinical evaluation; symptom patterns are not diagnostic criteria for the app. Sleep diary suggestions do not justify obsessive tracking or self-diagnosis.

claim_mappings.claim: The guideline emphasizes reviewing sleep disorders, daytime sleepiness, respiratory impairment, substance history, and medication interactions in clinical care.
claim_mappings.limitations: Professional clinical practice guideline intended to support clinician judgment, not replace it. The app must not diagnose, prescribe, or independently determine suitability for CBT-I, BBT-I, sleep restriction, or medication.

shared_safety_claims.claim: Structured insomnia behavioral interventions require clinician-led adaptation or delay in contexts such as excessive daytime sleepiness, nighttime fall risk or inability to transfer, active exposure-based PTSD treatment, bipolar disorder, uncontrolled seizures, medical instability, acute mental health symptoms, pregnancy/postpartum, or active substance use disorder.
shared_safety_claims.limitations: VA/DoD clinician guidance, not a self-screening tool. These conditions do not let the app determine treatment eligibility; they require qualified clinical assessment and individualized decisions.

shared_safety_claims.claim: Sleep restriction is a clinical behavioral intervention with population-specific cautions; the app must not prescribe sleep restriction or sleep deprivation.
shared_safety_claims.limitations: Adult chronic insomnia guideline; does not authorize unsupervised sleep restriction.
